question: Will Plus Ultra operate a scheduled Madrid–Lima passenger flight on 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Plus Ultra stopped selling MAD-LIM tickets on 13 Nov 2026 amid preconcurso and an ERE, intending to exit Lima, but as of 16 Nov no last-flight date has been set and flights continue on time (T News). Distressed carriers that pull sales usually fly already-sold tickets for a few weeks (rough 2-6 week wind-down, a recalled pattern, not a counted base rate), and Thursday remains a scheduled day after the Tue/Sat cuts. Against: strong incentive to cut losses fast under a 61% flight-hour cut, a precedent of cutting Buenos Aires flights in October without rebooking passengers, and the FR24 schedule seen only to 20 Nov. Net slightly above even. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- T News (16 Nov 2026): Plus Ultra Lima flights continue with normal punctuality; 'yesterday's flight departed and arrived on time'; date the airline will stop operating the route still unknown.
- T News (13 Nov 2026): sources have no tentative cessation date, whether days, weeks or months away; a PU flight left Madrid on time that day; July 2026 Lima traffic was a record 16,349 passengers.
- El Cronista (13 Nov 2026): sales halted for Buenos Aires and Lima; no official final operating date communicated; plan is a >61% cut in commercial flight hours, focusing on Venezuela plus charter/ACMI; fuel costs EUR104.8m vs EUR69.1m budgeted; Feb-Aug operating loss EUR31.08m.
- DeepArrival (13 Nov 2026): Lima became daily in July; flights no longer on sale; final dates not announced; airline did not answer questions about existing bookings.
- Que.es (15 Nov 2026): reservations on suspended routes require contacting the airline; preconcurso gives up to 6 months of legal margin; situation 'can change at any moment'.
- Search snippets (T News/aviation press): Lima Tuesday flights dropped from 13 Oct, Saturday flights dropped from 7 Nov -> 5 weekly (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun). 26 Nov 2026 is a Thursday.
- Flightmapper: PU301 schedule from 25 Oct 2026, Mon and Wed-Sun, dep 11:00 MAD; no end date shown (pre-dates the Saturday cut).
- Question background: as of 13 Nov, FR24 listed PU301 departures only up to 20 Nov (FR24 normally shows about a week ahead, so this may be the display horizon, not an end date).
- Infobae/iProfesional (Oct 2026): when Buenos Aires frequencies were cut, Plus Ultra offered no rebooking on other carriers, stranding 200+ passengers; precedent for cutting flights abruptly on short notice.
- Status quo as of 16 Nov: route operating normally, sales closed, no last date announced.
- Base rate: no published data found. A rough heuristic (recalled pattern, not counted) is that distressed carriers that stop selling a route often keep flying sold bookings for about 2-6 weeks; this case is about 13 days after the sales stop.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off Flightradar24 PU301 history for the 26 Nov (Madrid date) departure (fallback Airportia or credible sources), not off sales status or announcements.
- Event window: single scheduled departure on 26 Nov 2026 (Madrid date); as of 16 Nov 21:20Z, 10 days remain before the date.
- Searched but not found: an official last-flight date for Lima, a Plus Ultra press release, live FR24/Airportia schedule beyond 20 Nov (pages blocked), any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: Lima operating normally on 16 Nov, sales stopped 13 Nov, no last date, and Thursday still a scheduled day after the Tue/Sat cuts. The factual points (Thursday a scheduled day; the FR24 20-Nov listing being only its normal display window) agree across dossiers and are accepted. The RTVC 'stopped scheduling' wording is ambiguous: it also lists Venezuela, which others report still on sale, so it gets little weight. The remaining dispute is a judgment about how long the wind-down lasts. Fly-out-sold-inventory norms and refund costs favor YES; the cash crisis and abrupt-cut precedent favor NO. No web access on this run, so nothing new could be checked. I land slightly above even, in the middle of the run range, because that is where the evidence puts it and not as an average.
